---
title: Data analysis
description: Pandas and Matplotlib output rendered at build time.
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
data = pd.DataFrame({
    "group": np.repeat(["A", "B", "C"], 50),
    "value": np.concatenate([rng.normal(m, 1, 50) for m in (0, 1.5, 3)]),
})
```

## Summary table

```{python}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary statistics per group."
from IPython.display import Markdown

summary = data.groupby("group")["value"].agg(["mean", "std", "count"]).round(2)
Markdown(summary.to_markdown())
```

@tbl-summary summarises the simulated data.

## Distribution

```{python}
#| label: fig-hist
#| fig-cap: "Histogram of values per group."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))
for name, grp in data.groupby("group"):
    ax.hist(grp["value"], bins=15, alpha=0.6, label=name)
ax.legend()
plt.show()
```

The groups in @fig-hist are clearly shifted.
